name: Guinea
summary_text: Guinea is dangerous for trans visitors. The Penal Code criminalises same-sex conduct (3 years); a 2024 UPR stakeholder report documents violence and discrimination from both state and non-state actors; junta rule since 2021; no LGR.

sources.claim_summary: The Advocates for Human Rights: UPR stakeholder report on Guinea (Oct 2024) covering LGBTIQ+ rights — criminalisation ('against the order of nature', up to 3 years) and social context.

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Equatorial Guinea (listed under Guinea's picks): official assessment - same-sex conduct not specifically criminalised but LGBT persons face stigma; no anti-discrimination protections.

sources.title: Guinea - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Guinea: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised (Article 325, 'indecency' provisions); documents violence and discrimination against LGBT persons and police harassment.

The Advocates for Human Rights + Khaleem Ali joint UPR stakeholder report (Oct 2024) on LGBT+ rights in Guinea: criminalisation of consensual same-sex activity; police arbitrary arrests, harassment and extortion; a hostile and 'sometimes deadly' environment; widespread stigmatisation hinders reporting of violence.
US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Guinea: documents security-force torture, prison abuse, FGM, and the LGBT section noting criminalisation and societal discrimination.

US State Department 2012 Human Rights Report for Guinea-Bissau (listed under Guinea's picks): documents the 2012 coup, arbitrary killings, torture, impunity - general context; no criminalisation of same-sex conduct.
